title: Treat design as a bridge
principle: Design connects people to possibilities. Clarity of the crossing matters more than ornament on the railing.
procedure: Name who is crossing and what possibility waits on the other side.
Remove obstacles on the bridge (jargon, mystery controls, dead ends).
Make the next step obvious within one glance.
Ornament only if it helps orientation or trust.
Test with someone who wasn’t in the room.
examplePrompts:
Frame this flow as a bridge.

Who crosses: <…>
Possibility on the other side: <…>
Obstacles to remove: <…>
One-glance next step:
Ornament allowed only if it aids orientation.
promptWhy: Reframes UI as connection, not decoration.
tips: Shape of Design frames design as connection/bridge work.

workedExamples.title: Ornate dead end
workedExamples.after: One obvious crossing; beauty supports wayfinding.

antiPatterns: Designing only for people in the room.
